questions.question: By the 1970s, Public Sector Units (PSUs) had become dominant in the Indian industry. What criticism did they frequently face?

options.text: Excessive foreign ownership and capital outflow
High competition from private multinational corporations
Over-reliance on export markets for revenue
Operational inefficiencies, low productivity, and financial losses

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Operational inefficiencies, low productivity, and financial losses**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• By the 1970s, Public Sector Units (PSUs) in India had grown significantly, controlling key industries such as steel, coal, and heavy machinery.
 
• PSUs were frequently criticized for **operational inefficiencies**, which included excessive red tape, bureaucratic delays, and outdated technologies.
 
• Low productivity plagued many PSUs, as they often operated without stringent performance benchmarks and faced issues with workforce management.
 
• Financial losses became a recurring problem due to mismanagement, overstaffing, and a lack of focus on profitability.
 
• The dominance of PSUs also stifled competition, leading to monopolistic practices that further worsened efficiency and innovation in the industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public Sector Units (PSUs):**

 
 
• PSUs are government-owned corporations created to undertake commercial activities on behalf of the government.
 
• They played a key role in India’s planned economy post-independence, focusing on industrial development and self-reliance.
 
• Examples include Steel Authority of India (SAIL), Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL), and Indian Oil Corporation (IOC).
 
 
 
• **License Raj:**
 
 
• The License Raj was a system of elaborate licenses and regulations that governed the Indian economy from 1947 to 1991.
 
• This system restricted private sector growth and granted PSUs a dominant role in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Economic Reforms of 1991:**
 
 
• To address inefficiencies in the public sector, India initiated liberalization, privatization, and globalization (LPG) reforms.
 
• These reforms reduced the role of PSUs by encouraging private sector participation and reducing regulatory hurdles.
 
 
 
• **Disinvestment in PSUs:**
 
 
• Disinvestment refers to the process of selling or liquidating government-owned assets in PSUs.
 
• It was introduced to improve efficiency, reduce fiscal burden, and foster competition.

questions.question:
Which of the following correctly characterises the regulatory and structural aspects of the NPS Vatsalya scheme, as launched in 2024?

1. The scheme is administered by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).

2. Contributions under NPS Vatsalya are pooled into a government-managed consolidated fund without individual accounts.

3.The scheme allows a smooth shift to a regular NPS account when the subscriber turns 18 years of age.

4.Upon attaining adulthood, subscribers must compulsorily exit NPS Vatsalya and opt for the Atal Pension Yojana.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **NPS Vatsalya**, launched in 2024, is a child-focused pension scheme overseen by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).
 
• Under the scheme, children below 18 years of age can have individual accounts, allowing for targeted savings with flexible contributions.
 
• Subscribers are permitted a smooth transition to a regular NPS account upon reaching 18 years of age, ensuring continuity in retirement planning.
 
• Option 3 correctly highlights that the scheme is regulated by PFRDA and facilitates the seamless migration to a standard NPS account.
 
• Contrary to some options, the scheme does not mandate a switch to Atal Pension Yojana upon adulthood but ensures voluntary transitions based on subscriber needs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA):**

 
 
• PFRDA is a statutory authority under the Indian government responsible for regulating and promoting pension schemes such as the National Pension System (NPS).
 
• It plays a crucial role in ensuring the financial security of citizens post-retirement.
 
 
 
• **National Pension System (NPS):**
 
 
• NPS is a government-backed voluntary retirement savings scheme open to all Indian citizens aged 18-70.
 
• Subscribers can contribute regularly to their accounts and receive market-linked returns.
 
• NPS is managed by PFRDA and offers tax benefits under Section 80CCD(1) and 80CCD(1B).
 
 
 
• **Atal Pension Yojana (APY):**
 
 
• APY is a government-backed pension scheme focused on unorganized sector workers.
 
• It provides guaranteed pension benefits ranging from Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 5,000 per month, depending on contributions.
 
• Eligible subscribers must be between 18-40 years of age.
 
 
 
• **Child-Focused Financial Schemes:**
 
 
• Such schemes aim to inculcate early financial discipline and savings habits among children.
 
• They often include features like flexible contributions, parental oversight, and benefits tailored to future needs.

questions.question: On 26 February 2025, the Centre for Science and Environment (CSE) and Down To Earth (DTE) magazine released their annual publication 'State of India’s Environment' from which state?

• The annual publication 'State of India's Environment' was released on **26 February 2025** by the Centre for Science and Environment (CSE) and Down To Earth (DTE).
 
• This report provides an in-depth analysis of India’s environmental challenges and tracks the country's progress in addressing them.
 
• The publication was released from **Rajasthan**, which has often been at the forefront of environmental discussions due to its unique ecological challenges.
 
• The report covers topics such as climate change, air pollution, water resources, waste management, and biodiversity conservation.
 
• It serves as a critical resource for policymakers, researchers, and environmental advocates to understand and address pressing environmental issues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Centre for Science and Environment (CSE):**

 
 
• CSE is a public interest research and advocacy organization based in New Delhi, India.
 
• It focuses on sustainable development, climate change, environmental education, and policy analysis.
 
• Its mission is to promote equitable and sustainable use of natural resources and advocate for environmental justice.
 
 
 
• **Down To Earth (DTE):**
 
 
• DTE is a fortnightly magazine published by CSE, specializing in environmental, science, and development news.
 
• It provides insights into critical issues such as climate change, pollution, and resource management.
 
• The magazine is widely recognized for its investigative journalism and in-depth reports.
 
 
 
• **State of India's Environment Report:**
 
 
• The report is an annual publication by CSE and DTE, offering a comprehensive overview of India’s environmental status.
 
• It highlights trends, data, and analysis on key environmental issues affecting the country.
 
• The report serves as a benchmark for tracking progress in environmental conservation and sustainable development.
 
 
 
• **Rajasthan’s Environmental Context:**

• The state has implemented various initiatives, such as afforestation and water conservation programs, to address these issues.
 
• It is a significant location for discussions on sustainable development due to its ecological importance.

questions.question: Which of the following is INCORRECT based on the Supreme Court’s ruling in 'Samtola Devi vs The State Of Uttar Pradesh', on 27 March 2025, regarding the ‘Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007’?

options.text: The Act does not provide any provision for the eviction of a child or relative
Tribunals under the Act have the authority to order the eviction of a child or relative if it is deemed necessary for the protection of the senior citizen.
Eviction of a child or relative is mandatory in every case of neglect under the Act
Senior citizens can file for maintenance even after transferring their property to their legal heirs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eviction of a child or relative is mandatory in every case of neglect under the Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Supreme Court ruling in 'Samtola Devi vs The State Of Uttar Pradesh' (2025) clarified that eviction under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, is not mandatory in every case of neglect.
 
• The Act empowers tribunals to order eviction only if it is deemed necessary for the protection and welfare of the senior citizen involved.
 
• There is no blanket provision in the Act that mandates eviction in all cases of neglect by children or relatives.
 
• The Act also allows senior citizens to file for maintenance even after transferring their property to legal heirs.
 
• The Supreme Court emphasized that the Act's primary aim is to ensure the welfare and dignity of senior citizens, not punitive eviction measures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007:**

 
 
• This Act was enacted to ensure financial and emotional support for senior citizens and parents.
 
• It provides a mechanism for senior citizens to claim maintenance from their children or legal heirs.
 
• The Act also includes provisions for tribunals to address disputes and ensure quick resolution.
 
 
 
• **Eviction Provisions under the Act:**
 
 
• The Act does not explicitly mandate eviction but allows tribunals to order eviction if necessary to protect senior citizens.
 
• This power is often used in cases where senior citizens face harassment, abuse, or neglect.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court's Role:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court serves as the highest authority to interpret laws and clarify ambiguities in their implementation.
 
• In this case, the Court clarified that eviction should not be treated as mandatory in all neglect cases.
 
 
 
• **Rights of Senior Citizens:**
 
 
• Senior citizens can seek maintenance, protection, and remedies under the Act.
 
• They are also entitled to reclaim property or assets transferred under undue influence or in cases of neglect.

questions.question: In 2024, India became the world's top milk producer with a production of 239 million metric tons. Which government initiative significantly contributed to this achievement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rashtriya Gokul Mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) was launched in December 2014 under the National Programme for Bovine Breeding and Dairy Development by the Government of India.
 
• The mission primarily focuses on the conservation and development of indigenous bovine breeds to enhance milk productivity and profitability for dairy farmers.
 
• Under the mission, initiatives such as the establishment of Gokul Grams (integrated cattle care centers) have been implemented to ensure scientific management of livestock.
 
• The program provides financial assistance for the strengthening of bull mother farms, setting up of semen stations, and promoting artificial insemination to improve breed quality.
 
• RGM has played a significant role in boosting milk production in India, contributing to the country becoming the world's top milk producer in 2024.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **White Revolution**

 
 
• The White Revolution in India was initiated in 1970 under Operation Flood, led by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) and spearheaded by Dr. Verghese Kurien.
 
• It transformed India from a milk-deficient country into the largest producer of milk and dairy products globally.
 
• It introduced modern dairy farming techniques and enhanced rural incomes, making it a landmark in India's dairy sector.
 
 
 
• **National Dairy Development Program**
 
 
• This initiative aims to increase milk production and productivity by strengthening dairy infrastructure and providing technical support to farmers.
 
• It complements the Rashtriya Gokul Mission in achieving long-term sustainability in dairy farming.
 
 
 
• **Artificial Insemination in Livestock**
 
 
• Artificial insemination involves the manual introduction of semen into the female reproductive tract to ensure controlled and high-quality breeding.
 
• This technology is a cornerstone of the Rashtriya Gokul Mission, helping to improve the genetic traits of indigenous cattle breeds.
 
 
 
• **Indigenous Breeds of Cattle**
 
 
• India is home to several high-quality indigenous cattle breeds, such as Gir, Sahiwal, and Red Sindhi.
 
• These breeds are known for their adaptability, disease resistance, and significant contribution to milk production under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of 'Srjanam', the biomedical waste conversion system launched in 2025?

options.text: To develop a new method for incineration
To promote traditional biomedical waste disposal methods
To increase the use of landfills for biomedical waste
To reduce environmental hazards by eliminating incineration

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To reduce environmental hazards by eliminating incineration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'Srjanam'** is a biomedical waste conversion system launched in 2025, aimed at addressing environmental concerns arising from traditional waste disposal methods.
 
• The primary objective of the system is to **eliminate the use of incineration**, which is known to release harmful pollutants such as dioxins and furans into the environment.
 
• It focuses on converting biomedical waste into **eco-friendly byproducts** through advanced scientific techniques.
 
• The initiative is designed to **reduce landfill dependency** and promote sustainable waste management practices.
 
• By adopting innovative technology, 'Srjanam' seeks to **minimize environmental hazards** and align with global efforts to combat climate change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biomedical Waste:**

 
 
• Biomedical waste refers to waste generated during the diagnosis, treatment, or immunization of humans or animals.
 
• It includes sharps, infectious materials, pathological waste, and pharmaceutical waste.
 
• Improper disposal of biomedical waste poses risks to human health and the environment.
 
 
 
• **Incineration:**
 
 
• Incineration is a waste disposal method that involves burning materials at high temperatures.
 
• It is commonly used for biomedical waste but releases toxic emissions such as dioxins and furans.
 
• These pollutants are harmful to both humans and the environment.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Waste Management Practices:**
 
 
• These practices focus on reducing waste generation, recycling, and adopting eco-friendly disposal methods.
 
• Advanced technologies such as chemical treatment and plasma arc gasification are gaining traction.
 
 
 
• **Global Efforts to Reduce Waste Pollution:**
 
 
• The United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) emphasize responsible consumption and production to combat waste pollution.
 
• Countries worldwide are adopting stricter regulations and innovative solutions for waste management.

• This growing trend highlights the increasing reliance on self-employment as a primary source of livelihood for millions across India.
 
• Self-employment has been a dominant form of employment in rural areas, driven by agricultural activities and small-scale enterprises.
 
• The report also indicates a rise in self-employment in urban areas, attributed to the expansion of gig economy platforms and freelance opportunities.
 
• The surge in self-employment reflects the effectiveness of government initiatives like **Skill India, Start-Up India, and Mudra Yojana** in promoting entrepreneurship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-employment:**

 
 
• Refers to individuals working for themselves rather than being employed by a company or organization.
 
• Common examples include entrepreneurs, freelancers, small business owners, and independent contractors.
 
• It provides flexibility in work schedules but often comes with challenges like income variability and lack of social security benefits.
 
 
 
• **Economic Survey Report:**
 
 
• An annual document presented by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India.
 
• Provides detailed analysis of the country's economic performance and key trends over the past year.
 
• Serves as a crucial input for formulating policies and budgetary allocations.
 
 
 
• **Entrepreneurship Trends in India:**
 
 
• India has seen a rapid rise in entrepreneurship due to digital penetration and government support.
 
• Initiatives like Start-Up India and Mudra Yojana aim to provide financial and infrastructural support to budding entrepreneurs.
 
• The gig economy has further empowered individuals to monetize their skills independently.

• **Skill India:** Focuses on skill development to enhance employability.

questions.question: As per World Bank’s State of Social Protection Report 2025, between 2010 and 2022, social protection coverage in low- and middle-income countries increased from 41% to ______.
questions.solution:

• Social protection programs often include **cash transfers, unemployment benefits, health insurance, and pensions**, which are crucial for reducing poverty and inequality.
 
• The increase in social protection coverage reflects **global initiatives** aimed at achieving **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly Goal 1 (No Poverty) and Goal 10 (Reduced Inequalities).
 
• The rise to **51%** underscores the importance of **government policies, international aid, and community-based programs** in addressing social and economic challenges.
 
• This progress is particularly significant for countries in regions like **Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Latin America**, which often face higher poverty rates.
 
• The report highlights the role of organizations like the **World Bank**, **UNICEF**, and other global entities in supporting social protection frameworks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Social Protection Coverage**__

 __
 
• **Social protection** refers to programs designed to reduce poverty and vulnerability by promoting efficient labor markets and diminishing people's exposure to risks.
 
• Examples include **conditional cash transfers, food assistance programs, old-age pensions, and disaster relief funds.**
 
• It is critical for achieving **inclusive economic growth** and protecting against economic shocks.
 
 
 
• **World Bank Reports**__
 
 
• The **World Bank** publishes periodic reports to assess progress in areas such as **economic development, poverty alleviation, and social protection.**
 
• The **State of Social Protection Report** provides insights into global trends and challenges in expanding coverage.
 
• This report serves as a benchmark for policymakers to evaluate their strategies and improve their frameworks.

questions.question: What was the poverty headcount ratio in urban areas in 2019-21, as per the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**5.27%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2023** is based on data from the **NFHS-5 (2019-21)**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding the 2024 Haryana Assembly elections are correct?

1. The BJP formed the government for a third consecutive term in Haryana.

2. The Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) secured 2 seats in the election.

3. Independent candidates secured more than 5 seats in the assembly.

4. The majority mark in the Haryana Legislative Assembly was 48 seats.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **2024 Haryana Assembly Elections**, the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** formed the government for the **third consecutive term** in the state. ***Hence, Statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **Indian National Lok Dal (INLD)** secured **2 seats** in the Haryana Legislative Assembly elections. ***Hence, Statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Independent candidates** did not secure more than **5 seats** in the election. ***Hence, Statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Haryana Legislative Assembly** has a total of **90 seats**, and the majority mark required to form the government is **46 seats**, not 48. ***Hence, Statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement-wise Analysis:**
 
 
• **1. BJP formed the government for a third consecutive term** – Correct.
 
• **2. INLD secured 2 seats** – Correct.
 
• **3. Independent candidates secured more than 5 seats** – Incorrect.
 
• **4. Majority mark was 48 seats** – Incorrect.
 
 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Only 1 and 2.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Haryana Legislative Assembly** is a **unicameral legislature** consisting of **90 elected members**.
 
• The term of the Haryana Assembly is generally **5 years** unless dissolved earlier.
 
• **Chandigarh** serves as the capital of both **Haryana** and **Punjab**.
 
• **Indian National Lok Dal (INLD)** is a regional political party mainly active in Haryana and was founded by **Devi Lal**.
 
• The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** conducts Assembly elections under the provisions of the **Constitution of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **majority mark** in any legislative assembly is calculated as **more than half** of the total seats.
 
• Questions related to **recent elections, constitutional bodies, political parties, and state legislatures** are frequently asked in competitive examinations.

questions.question: Which international event focused on climate change was held in Baku, Azerbaijan, in November 2024?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**COP29**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **COP29** refers to the 29th annual Conference of the Parties under the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)**.
 
• The event is scheduled to take place in **Baku, Azerbaijan, in November 2024**.
 
• COP29 serves as a significant platform where world leaders, policymakers, and environmental experts come together to address climate
